{"summary": "Implemented set_left_most_unset_bit by setting the most significant zero bit within the binary representation (extending to the next bit when all bits are set) and added tests covering the example and edge cases.", "files": {"solution.py": """"Write a python function to set the left most unset bit."""


def set_left_most_unset_bit(n):
    """Set the left most unset bit of ``n`` and return the result.

    The search is over the bits of the binary representation of ``n``
    (without leading zeros), scanning from the most significant bit
    towards the least significant bit. The first ``0`` found is set
    to ``1``; all other bits are unchanged. If the representation
    contains no ``0`` (i.e. ``n`` is of the form ``2**k - 1``), the
    unset bit immediately to the left of the most significant bit is
    set, so e.g. ``15`` (``1111``) becomes ``31`` (``11111``). As a
    consequence of the same rule, ``0`` becomes ``1``.

    Args:
        n: A non-negative integer.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``n`` is negative.
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n must be non-negative")

    width = n.bit_length()
    all_ones = (1 << width) - 1

    if n == all_ones:
        # No unset bit within the representation (this also handles
        # n == 0, whose width is 0): set the next bit to the left.
        return n | (1 << width)

    unset_bits = (~n) & all_ones
    left_most_unset_position = unset_bits.bit_length() - 1
    return n | (1 << left_most_unset_position)

def _reference(n):
    bits = bin(n)[2:]
    index = bits.find("0")
    if index == -1:
        return int("1" + bits, 2)
    return int(bits[:index] + "1" + bits[index + 1 :], 2)


def test_matches_reference_for_range():
    for n in range(256):
        assert set_left_most_unset_bit(n) == _reference(n)


def test_only_one_previously_unset_bit_is_set():
    for n in range(256):
        result = set_left_most_unset_bit(n)
        changed = result ^ n
        assert result | n == result  # no set bit is cleared
        assert changed & (changed - 1) == 0  # exactly one bit changed
        assert changed & n == 0  # the changed bit was previously unset
